column3: Establishes divine sovereignty over east and west beyond any single direction.

Parallels the focus on divinely authorized right direction, but without qibla specifics.
Frames guidance as God's call to a straight way, a general parallel.
Gives the commanded new qibla and its application wherever believers are.
Offers only a general statement that God's path is straight.

Sets refusal to follow the qibla against following desires after knowledge.

Connects clear signs with divine guidance to a straight path.
Adds that some recipients of Scripture recognize the truth yet conceal it.

Universal mortality adds no material interpretive value here.

Completes the House prayer with a messenger who teaches, purifies, and guides the community.

Commands believers to obey God and the Messenger rather than turn away while hearing.

Commands steadfast uprightness as ordered, a practical counterpart to remaining aligned.

Names a prophetic path grounded in insight and exclusive devotion to God.
Connects Abraham, the sacred town, and distance from idols.
Places Abraham's offspring near the Sacred House for establishing prayer.

Connects exclusive worship of God with establishing prayer for remembrance.
Makes following divine guidance the boundary between guidance and going astray.
States the shared prophetic summons to worship God alone.
Links divinely guided leadership with performing prayer and giving alms.

Defines the faithful response to God and the Messenger as hearing and obeying.
Regulates engagement with People of the Book through shared submission to the one God.
Promises guidance in God's paths to those who strive for Him.
Commands turning back to God while maintaining reverence and prayer.
Commands setting the face toward the upright religion before the decisive day.
Uses submission of one's face to God and good action as holding the firmest handhold.
Denies believers an independent choice once God and the Messenger decide a matter.
Names the revealed message as truth that guides to the path of the Mighty and Praised.
Commands worship of God with religion made sincere to Him.
Restates the command to worship God with sincere religious devotion.
Contrasts avoiding false worship with turning back to God.
Links an opened heart for submission with light from its Lord.
Calls to the one God and commands uprightness toward Him.
Pairs declaring God as Lord with steadfastness, a durable alignment parallel.
Unifies Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus under established religion and rejects division in it.
Commands uprightness, impartiality, and refusal to follow desires amid religious disagreement.
Places the Messenger on a divinely given way and forbids following the desires of the ignorant.
Treats allegiance to the Messenger as allegiance to God and makes fidelity consequential.
Contrasts obedience to the Messenger with hardship and praises faith made beloved in hearts.
Contrasts conjecture and desire with guidance that has come from the Lord.
Presents Abraham and his companions as a model of exclusive allegiance to God.
